key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powder that is amorphous after 800 °C treatment and becomes crystalline quartz/cristobalite after 1200 °C annealing.
engineering_relevance: This offers a low-cost, waste-derived feedstock for thermal spray powder development, with phase control enabling tuning of coating precursor properties.
method: Chemically treat rice husk ash to extract SiO2.
Heat treat the extracted material at 800 °C for 3 h to obtain amorphous silica.
Anneal at 1200 °C to induce crystallization into quartz and cristobalite.
evidence_signal: XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction showed an amorphous product with D50 ≈ 88.9 μm, then phase transformation to quartz and cristobalite after higher-temperature annealing.
watch_item: The particle size is relatively coarse for many spray processes, so additional milling/classification may be needed before practical thermal spray use.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
